question: Which English fast bowler was awarded a knighthood in April 2025 after retiring with a record 704 Test wickets, making him England’s all-time leading wicket-taker in Test cricket?
solution:
The correct answer is __**James Anderson**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **James Anderson** is England’s most successful Test bowler, with a record of **704 Test wickets** as of his retirement in April 2025, making him the all-time leading wicket-taker for England in Test cricket.
 
• He was awarded a **knighthood** in April 2025 for his exceptional contributions to cricket, recognizing his longevity, skill, and impact on the game.
 
• Anderson made his Test debut for England in **2003** and became one of the most consistent performers in international cricket, known for his mastery of swing bowling.
 
• He is the **first fast bowler** in the history of cricket to surpass 700 Test wickets, a milestone achieved in the twilight years of his career.
 
• His career spanned over two decades, during which he played a pivotal role in England’s success, including their famous **Ashes victories** and other memorable Test wins.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **James Anderson's Career Highlights:**

 
 
• Born on **July 30, 1982**, in Burnley, Lancashire, England.
 
• Known for his exceptional ability to swing the ball both ways, particularly in English conditions, making him one of the most feared bowlers in Test cricket.
 
• He has played a total of **179 Test matches**, the most by any fast bowler in cricket history.
 
• Anderson has taken **32 five-wicket hauls** and 3 ten-wicket hauls in Test matches.
 
 
 
• **Stuart Broad:**
 
 
• Another legendary English fast bowler, Broad retired in **2023** with over 600 Test wickets, making him the second-highest wicket-taker for England after Anderson.
 
• Known for his fiery spells, Broad’s career also featured memorable performances in the Ashes series.
 
 
 
• **Andrew Flintoff:**
 
 
• Flintoff was a charismatic all-rounder who played for England between 1998 and 2009.
 
• While he contributed with both bat and ball, he did not achieve the longevity or wicket tally of Anderson and Broad.
 
 
 
• **Darren Gough:**
 
 
• Gough was a prominent England fast bowler in the 1990s and early 2000s, known for his reverse swing and aggressive bowling style.
 
• He retired with **229 Test wickets**, but his career was not as statistically dominant as Anderson’s.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Knighthood for Cricketers:**

 
 
• Knighthood is one of the highest civilian honors in the UK, awarded for exceptional achievements in various fields, including sports.
 
• Previous cricketers knighted include **Sir Ian Botham, Sir Alastair Cook, and Sir Geoffrey Boycott**.
 
 
 
• **Fast Bowling Records:**
 
 
• Anderson is the **leading wicket-taker among all fast bowlers** in Test cricket history, surpassing legends like Glenn McGrath and Courtney Walsh.
 
• He is fourth on the overall list of wicket-takers, behind spinners like Muttiah Muralitharan, Shane Warne, and Anil Kumble.
